title: Theology close
hookLine: belief is reasoned about, but lived in the heart
tomorrow: I was sent to perfect character

lines: FAITH HAS TO ENTER THE HEART.
cards: Some desert Arabs came to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and announced: we believe. The Qur'an records the answer he was told to give, gentle but firm. Don't say you believe.
Say you've submitted. Faith hasn't yet entered your hearts. It's a striking line to end a block of theology on.
For weeks we've talked about what Muslims believe and how theologians argued about it, and here the Qur'an says belief isn't finished when you can say it. It has to go somewhere.

teach.h: SIX ARTICLES, THE THEOLOGIANS, THE UNSEEN.
teach.b: Look back at the road. The block opened with the six articles of faith: Allah the One, the angels, the books, the messengers, the Last Day, and the decree.
Then the theologians: kalam, the Mu'tazilah and their justice, the trial over the created Qur'an, al-Ash'ari and al-Maturidi, the Athari approach, Shia theology, and the hard question of suffering.

Then the unseen journey: death and return, the grave, the questions, the trumpet, the gathering, the book, the scale, the bridge, and this week, the intercession, the pool, the fire, the garden, seeing Him, and mercy in a hundred parts.
The theologians argued hard, and well, and disagreed in earnest, and their work is still studied. But the verse about the desert Arabs puts it in its place.
Saying it is one step. Faith entering the heart is another. A hadith in Sahih Muslim gives the other half.
Faith, the Prophet said, has many branches. The highest is saying there is no god but Allah.

teach.h: FROM A CREED TO A ROCK IN THE ROAD.
teach.b: The lowest is moving something harmful out of the road. And modesty is a branch of faith too. The top branch is a creed.
The bottom branch is a rock on a path, moved so nobody trips. That's the bridge to the next block.
Belief is reasoned about, but lived. Starting tomorrow, the path turns inward, to character and the heart's stations: what belief looks like in a person.

how: Muslims study the articles of faith and the questions of theology, and teachers also stress that faith shows in deeds; Muslims may also pray two voluntary rak'ahs outside the five daily prayers.

o: a debate where theologians finally all came to agree
the end of the belief block: faith reasoned about, then lived
the last prayer of the day, said just before going to sleep

games.q: the theology close — tap the pairs.
p: Allah, angels, books, messengers, Day, decree
there is no god but Allah
moving harm out of the road

s: in the Qur'an, saying 'we believe' settles the matter of faith
the desert Arabs were told faith had not yet entered their hearts.
the hadith counts moving something harmful from the road as a branch of faith
it names it as the lowest branch, with saying there is no god but Allah as the highest.
modesty is named in the hadith as a branch of faith
the same hadith says modesty is a branch of faith.

games.q: you've just told the Prophet: we believe. what does the Qur'an have him answer?
o: say rather: we submit; faith has not yet entered your hearts.
games.why: the answer is gentle but firm: belief has to enter the heart, not only the mouth.

practice: If you pray, you can pray two voluntary rak'ahs now, slowly, as you've been taught, letting each movement carry what this block taught you.
If you don't pray, or can't right now, sit quietly and let one belief from these weeks come to mind.
Then ask one plain question: where would this show up in my hands, a hand on a door, a word to a neighbor, a rock moved off a path?

wordCard.voice: Theology close. The end of a block on belief: the articles, the theologians, the unseen journey, and a reminder that faith is reasoned about, but has to be lived. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: faith; the word the desert Arabs claimed too soon.

carryVoice: Your line: believe, and live it. A creed at the top, a rock moved from the road at the bottom. Tomorrow, a new block begins.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 9; Sahih Muslim 35 (the branches of faith; removing harm from the road; modesty)
Sahih Muslim 8 (the six articles of faith, in the hadith of Jibril)
